notes: Sibling of CI-2026-08-09-POST-FREEZE-OBSERVER-REVIEW-001 (that rule governs how N observers decide against a frozen artifact; this rule governs how a live-query-derived REPORT about that same frozen artifact may claim to represent it at all).

Generalizes beyond crystals: any surface that reports 'what a frozen/committed object contained' from a LIVE query over mutable storage — rather than a persisted snapshot — carries the same risk, and the same fix (recompute the same commitment, compare, refuse on mismatch) applies wherever the query and the commitment share one deterministic projection.

canaries.assertion: buildFrozenCrystalManifest verifies by recomputing the SAME frozenHash projection crystalStatistics.ts uses and comparing it to the persisted artifact.contentHash; on a match it serves full member detail with verifiedAgainstFreeze:true; on a mismatch (simulated corpus drift) it withholds members (null) and intraCrystalEdges (null) rather than serving the live query as the frozen set; never exposes creatorAliasCommitment; honestly reports freeze-ceremony disclosure fields as never persisted rather than recomputing them as if they were.

statement: A report that claims to describe an already-frozen/committed object, but is actually computed from a live, mutable query, must recompute the SAME deterministic commitment the freeze act pinned and compare it before serving detail — and must refuse to serve that detail as authoritative when the comparison fails, rather than silently substituting current state for the frozen fact.

occurrences.defect: No hash-verified per-invariant manifest existed for a frozen crystal; the only persisted fact was a content hash, with no reader that checked a live re-query against it before presenting member detail as the frozen set.
